about.title: A Village in Its Own Words
paragraphs: Bandwar is a village in the Begusarai district of Bihar, part of the historic Mithila region. It sits along the flood-prone Burhi Gandak river — a fact that has shaped its name, its architecture, and its people.
This portal is a community-built record of the village. It is not a government project, a political platform, or a commercial venture. It is a record of a village, kept by the village.
Every article, every photograph, every fact — contributed or verified by residents of Bandwar and their descendants.

principles.title: Non-political
principles.description: We don't endorse parties or candidates. Achievements are credited by name; failures are documented by fact. Never by affiliation.

principles.title: Every fact is sourced
principles.description: Nothing published without a source — public record, resident verification, or personal observation.

principles.title: Nothing without consent
principles.description: Every photograph, memory, and contribution is published only with the explicit consent of the person who shared it.

principles.title: Community-led
principles.description: This isn't a government project. It isn't a commercial venture. It's a record of a village, kept by the village.

principles.title: Free & open
principles.description: The portal is free to use, and the code is open source. Anyone can adapt it for their own village.

sources.name: News18, Prabhat Khabar, Hindustan, Dainik Jagran

community.lead: The Bandwar Portal is maintained by a committee of residents, former residents, and their descendants. It is a volunteer effort — no one is paid, and nothing is published for profit.
community.contributors: Every photograph, memory, and document shared with the portal is credited by name. Over 40 residents and descendants have contributed since 2024.
